newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips pause after big rally, Nasdaq racks up gain.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips pause after big rally, Nasdaq racks up gain.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Wednesday, one day after the Dow posted its second largest daily gain ever, while the Nasdaq market shook off its recent bearish trend to end higher.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed 20.87 points lower at 6,812.72. The Nasdaq Composite index rose 14.40 points at 1,227.14.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,330 to 1,136 on moderately active volume of 489 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts said investors turned cautious after propelling the Dow 173 points higher Tuesday, which was second in point terms only to the 187-point leap that came two days after the "Black Monday" stock market crash of Oct. 19, 1987.
Technology stocks, however, were led higher by sharp gains in market pacesetters such as International Business Machines Corp., Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp.
Earnings reports again dominated the session, with the big-name technology rally in particular linked to anticipation that IBM would release upbeat first quarter numbers after the close.
IBM, which rose 2-3/8 to 142-3/8 to lead all Dow gainers on the day, did not disappoint with its earnings of $1.19 billion, matching the very highest of Wall Street estimates.
Intel jumped 5 to 146-1/8 and Microsoft rallied 4-1/2 to 115-1/8. But once again, investor caution kept buying interest largely contained to the biggest, best-known names.

"We're not setting the world on fire," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. "It's a nervous kind of market and when people do come back in, they want to be in high-grade, liquid issues."
As has often been the case during the Dow's recent run, market breadth was fairly weak, with declining stocks outnumbering those that rose.
Analysts said the narrow buying indicated that investors continue to hold broad reservations about some basic issues facing the market, particularly interest rates.
The 30-year Treasury bond was off one-half point, raising its yield to 7.08 percent from 7.04 percent at Tuesday's close. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
Analysts said that once the flow of earnings reports ebbs, interest rate worries would likely once again grip the market.
"Next week, when the focus shifts from earnings, I think the market is going to go down," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers.

Shulman said he expected interest rates would soon be headed higher, with the 30-year bond yield rising to 7.50 percent. "That's not going to be friendly for stocks," he said. Long-term interest rates above 7 percent tend to draw money away stocks and into bonds.

Until then, however, earnings remain the dominant theme. Strong quarterly results from US Airways Group Inc. propelled that company to a 5-1/4 point surge to 34-1/8, leading a broad advance in trasportation stocks.
American Airlines parent company AMR Corp. rose 3 to 91-7/8 and Delta Air Lines Inc. added 2-3/4 to finish at 98-1/8.
Reader's Digest Association Inc. slumped 2-3/8 to 23-5/8 after it reported weak third quarter results.
VeriFone Inc. jumped 17-1/8 to 47-1/4 after agreeing to be acquired by Hewlett-Packard Co. Hewlett-Packard, which will swap one of its shares for each of VeriFone's shares, fell 1-1/8 to 49-3/8.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 0.97 points to 773.64. The American Stock Exchange index fell 1.60 to 543.36.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 1.13 to 404.71. The average share was down 11 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,296.894 off 3.393 or 0.05 percent.
